steps.body: Once the object is covered, the length is simply the number of units used. Count them carefully, one per placement.
steps.narration: Once the object is covered, the length is simply the number of units used. Count them carefully, one per placement.

widget.prompt: Cover this branch with one-unit blocks and count them as you go.
widget.successFeedback: Five blocks cover the branch — so the branch is five units long.
widget.alignFeedback: Line up zero with the object's starting end before measuring.
widget.gapOverlapFeedback: The blocks must touch end to end — no spaces and no covering the same part twice.
widget.unitFeedback: Every block must be the same size, or the count means nothing.

predict.prompt: Five same-size units exactly cover an object. How long is it?
predict.reveal: Length in units is the number of units it takes to cover the object — here, five.

cml.actionGoal: Manipulate the model and track how it represents g1m count units.
invariants: The manipulated model and the measurement relationship for g1m count units must stay consistent.
misconceptions: Reading a length from appearance or position instead of from same-size units laid end to end.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: What change would make the model stop representing the same measurement?

widget.prompt: Exactly 6 same-size cubes cover a ribbon with no gaps and no overlaps. How long is the ribbon in cubes?

options.feedback: Correct — the length is the number of same-size units that cover it end to end, which is 6.
That counts one unit more than were actually placed along the object.
That misses one of the units that helped cover the object.
That doubles the count, as if each unit were counted twice over.
